# Lenz 0.0.20 beta

This release refines Lenz Code's folder trust and fixes conflict handling on older git (PR #58). Updating is recommended.

- In the Folder Trust dialog, Tab then Enter trusts, in the desktop and terminal apps. Enter and Escape alone still stay restricted, and any other key, typed text or paste moves the focus back to Stay Restricted. The terminal app no longer takes Alt+T or Alt+P; the desktop app keeps them.
- Trust Parent Folder is no longer offered for the home folder, the folders above it, or folders other users can write to.
- An answer for a folder now replaces earlier answers for the folders inside it: trusting a folder you had kept restricted works, and restricting a folder also stops trusting the folders inside it.
- A project's own programs (TypeScript `tsc`, Go, Ruby and Python environments, ERB and Haml formatters) are looked for only inside the trusted folder that covers the project, even when a larger folder is open.
- The dialog asks only about tools inside the open folder. A tool held back elsewhere says to open its folder.
- A trust change made in another Lenz Code window applies within a few seconds, or when you switch to the window.
- Some tools read configuration above a trusted folder on their own (Cargo, RuboCop, Gradle, Maven, Node). Trust a folder only if you also trust the folders above it.
- Re-open in the conflict list works on git before 2.43 after Mark resolved as Delete or Keep.

## Validation

The release commit passes the full local Linux gate and `scripts/perf-check.sh`. The core tests also pass on git 2.30 (`scripts/ci-local.sh --old-git`). Native macOS interaction and git versions between 2.30 and 2.56 remain unverified. Native package build/signature and CLI checks are separate from interactive validation. macOS packages are ad-hoc signed.

Keep all five executables together. Verify the matching `.sha256` sidecar before installation.

[Changes since 0.0.19](https://github.com/aantoniadis/lenz/compare/v0.0.19...v0.0.20).
